title: Rust: Advanced Pattern Matching
description: Use advanced pattern matching features: destructuring, guards, and @ bindings.

steps.title: Destructuring Structs
steps.description: Define a struct `Point { x: i32, y: i32 }`. Use `let Point { x, y } = point;` to destructure. Print x and y separately.
hints: `let Point { x, y } = p;` destructures the fields.
Or match: `match p { Point { x, y } => println!("({}, {})", x, y) }`

verification.failureMessage: Destructure a Point and print x and y.

steps.title: Destructuring Enums
steps.description: Define `enum Message { Quit, Move { x: i32, y: i32 }, Write(String), ChangeColor(i32, i32, i32) }`. Write a function `process(msg: Message)` that handles each variant differently. Test with all variants.
hints: `Match { x, y } => println!("Move to ({}, {})", x, y)`
`ChangeColor(r, g, b) => println!("Color: {},{},{}", r, g, b)`

verification.failureMessage: Process all 4 Message variants and print their data.

steps.title: Match Guards
steps.description: Match on a number `x`: if x is positive and even → "positive even", if positive → "positive", if negative → "negative", if zero → "zero". Use match guards with `if`.
hints: Guards add extra conditions to match arms.
Order matters: more specific guards first.

verification.failureMessage: Match a number with guards and print the description.

steps.title: @ Bindings
steps.description: Use `@` bindings to bind a value while also pattern matching on it. Match a number: if in range 1..=5 → print the value and "small", if in 6..=10 → print and "medium". Use `num @ 1..=5`.
hints: `@` binds the value to a variable while also matching the pattern.
This is useful when you need both the value and structural match.

verification.failureMessage: Match a number with @ bindings and print its value and size.

steps.title: Match on References
steps.description: Match on a reference to an Option: create `let x = Some(42); let ref_x = &x;`. Match on `ref_x` and extract the inner value without moving. Print the matched value.
hints: Val is `&i32` in this context (reference to the inner value).

verification.failureMessage: Match on a reference to Option and print the value.
